name: claude-agent-scaffolding
description: Personal plugin marketplace for agent-assisted development: dual-repo workspace bootstrap, a skeleton-first delivery lifecycle, anti-sycophancy design critique, strict code-quality and architecture review, configuration security auditing, and decision-making mentor surfaces. Described by capability rather than by plugin name, so it does not go stale as plugins land.

plugins.name: workspace-init
plugins.description: Bootstrap or pair a dual-repo workspace (AI workspace + canonical), write pairing topology, install AI-trace commit-msg filters, and hand lifecycle work to ossify. Supports fresh bootstrap, a new AI workspace beside an existing canonical, and pairing two existing repositories.

plugins.name: ai-mentor
plugins.description: Decision-making mentor. Four skills auto-invoke on natural-language triggers: grill-me (one-question-at-a-time plan interrogation with CORE posture + 4 cognitive-discipline escape valves), council (5-persona multi-angle idea validation, Karpathy LLM Council pattern with codebase-aware Historian), eli10 (repeatable simplification), fool (sticky beginner's-mind mode). Skill-first; no hooks, no state.

plugins.name: architect-critic
plugins.description: Anti-sycophancy reviewer (skill-first). 6 skills auto-invoke on natural-language triggers: critiquing-spec (audit + sequential rebuttal with T=4 concession scoring), managing-async-critique (background Codex audits: status/result/cancel/resume), checking-adversary-readiness (doctor), reviewing-critique-history, listing-principles, promoting-principle. Ships ghost-notes (Wald survivor-bias) + CORE protocol (Curiosity/Objectivity/Reassurance/Empathy) as default principles. Principle promotion is manual (/promote-principle). Codex 0.125+ adversarial fresh-frame at close-depth, synchronous OR async. Standalone-invocable; other skills can invoke it in-conversation (no file IPC).

plugins.name: claude-security-audit
plugins.description: Static-analysis security audit for Claude Code project configurations and enabled plugins. 28 rules across 7 aspects: secrets (Anthropic/OpenAI/GitHub/AWS keys, JWTs, env-var leaks, base64 blobs), permissions (broad-allow, missing-deny, settings.local divergence, PERM-005 schema-typo validation, dangerous combos), hooks (curl|bash, rm -rf, unbounded eval, network exfiltration), MCP (untrusted endpoints, missing auth, env-var leaks), CLAUDE.md (plaintext secrets, internal markers), prompt-injection in agents/commands (common patterns; AST is v0.2), marketplace (untrusted sources, malformed manifest). Two-flag auto-fix (T2-H) gated on `RULE_AUTO_FIXABLE` + `RULE_MECHANICALLY_FIXABLE` with 5-layer defense-in-depth (rule re-validation, target re-resolution, symlink refusal, path-traversal refusal, atomic state log). Durable `finding_uid` (T2-I) survives whitespace/line-drift edits; baseline diff tags NEW vs PERSISTED. Self-tamper detection (T1-F) on state.json + suppressions.json. Critical-cannot-suppress + 60s race-window refusal. Zero ambient surface by default — SessionStart reminder ships as opt-in file (T1-C). Inspired by AgentShield in Everything Claude Code (Mustafa, 2026; MIT) — independent MIT implementation tailored to composable plugin marketplaces.

plugins.name: ossify
plugins.description: Skeleton-first delivery lifecycle from Release 0 through MVP and v1. workspace-init is optional as of 1.3.0: /ossify:start and /ossify:adopt author .ossify/topology.json themselves, reading a workspace-init pairing.json as a translated fallback only when one exists. 14 native skills (start, adopt, plan-release, plan-spine, run-spine, doctor, work-item, close, challenge, wayfinder, patch, handoff, handoff-resume, work-pr), 14 slash commands, and an implementer subagent. Self-sufficient since 1.1.0: the grill and the adversarial critic ship in-tree as /ossify:challenge, with a configurable external adversary. /ossify:start does the pre-code spec-core onboarding and /ossify:adopt onboards a project that already has code (six fail-closed gates, six conversions, Release 0 closed retroactively); /ossify:plan-release opens a release and /ossify:plan-spine lays out its skeleton; /ossify:run-spine drives a planned spine round by round, and since 1.8.0 accepts an optional --external-executor flag that hands each round's work items to a caller-supplied, provider-neutral in-session procedure (one request record out per item, one result record back) instead of dispatching the nested implementer subagent — the no-flag command is unchanged; /ossify:close runs the close ceremony with memory harvest; /ossify:doctor diagnoses state, spec, rules, interop, budgets and plugin provenance. /ossify:wayfinder (new at 1.2.0) charts a question into decision tickets on the issue tracker and works an existing map's frontier one ticket per session. /ossify:patch (new at 1.13.0) ships a defect in shipped behaviour, or a small request another project cannot fake, as a versioned patch off the default branch — a running spine is never reopened for it. /ossify:handoff, /ossify:handoff-resume, /ossify:work-pr and /ossify:wayfinder run standalone on any gh repo. Since 1.14.0 /ossify:run-spine re-enters a started spine on its own, at a round barrier or mid-round, printing a reconcile read-out and halting before any mutation on state it cannot reconcile. Since 1.26.0 `--external-executor --detach` ends the lane after it writes a round's requests and leaves counting, close and merge to the caller; `/close <wi-id> --pr` opens the item's PR; re-entry reads an item with a recorded PR as in flight.

plugins.name: code-judo
plugins.description: Strict quality review and architecture deepening. 4 prose skills, 4 slash commands, no runtime library. deep-review is a human-invoked maintainability audit of a diff or branch — the code-judo ambition standard (restructurings that delete complexity rather than rearrange it), the 1000-line rule with its waiver path, spaghetti-growth suspicion, wrapper/cast/boundary rules, a 7-tier prioritized output order, and a categorical approval bar with 6 presumptive blockers. It produces one report and one disposition pass and never re-reviews its own fixes; its verdict is advisory, never a merge gate. deepen-architecture scans a codebase for shallow modules using the deletion test, writes a single HTML report to the OS temp dir with before/after diagrams and Strong/Worth-exploring/Speculative badges, opens it in the browser, and grills through the candidate you pick. codebase-design ships the deep-module vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality), the four dependency categories, seam discipline, and design-it-twice. domain-modeling keeps the CONTEXT.md glossary where nothing else owns the project's vocabulary, and composes ADRs without filing them — the ADR directory is a numbered sequence and it leaves that to whichever plugin owns it. No hard cross-plugin dependencies: the grilling step resolves softly to ossify:challenge, then ai-mentor:grill-me, then an in-plugin protocol. Adapted from Cursor's thermo-nuclear code-quality review and Matt Pocock's improve-codebase-architecture.

plugins.name: crew
plugins.description: The orchestrator/worker session model over herdr or Orca, the project file's declared layer. An orchestrator session keeps its context for decisions and dispatches everything else to worker sessions launched by seat name: the operator's own files name each seat (~/.claude/crew/agents.md on the machine, .crew/roles.md in the project), implementers route by complexity class, one reviewer session runs its review command (/code-review by default) once per PR, the retained implementer works GitHub threads to zero, merge only on the operator's word. A session budget caps each work item at one implementer and one verifier. Each seat gets its own labelled tab holding one full-size pane, in the tree its --cwd names, so a run of five seats is five readable tabs. Readiness is derived, not declared: a seat herdr detects waits on a typed agent state, a seat it does not waits on a screen pattern, so an undetected agent CLI is a first-class seat and a detection manifest later upgrades it with no edit. A run's state lives in a dagr run.json the plugin owns and no binary writes. One fail-open hook tells a seat its own context figure past a configurable ceiling (default 500000 tokens) — a coordinator seat rotates on it, a leaf finishes; where molt runs, a child hands off to its parent and the top molts in place. Defers every other layer command to that layer's own guide. No lib, no state.

plugins.name: merge-bar
plugins.description: The pull-request lifecycle against a merge bar fixed when the PR opens. Open a PR whose body carries seven fields (Claim, Scope, Known limits, Merge danger, Merge bar, Evidence, Closes); work it by sorting every reviewer finding as blocking or non-blocking against that bar, one push per round, with a stop at round 3 when the fixes are generating the findings, and non-blocking findings answered in the thread or recorded as known limits in the paired AI workspace's tech-debt ledger instead of filed as issues; and teach a repository's reviewers the bar through an AGENTS.md Code Review Rules section and, on public repositories, a .coderabbit.yaml. Three prose skills, three slash commands, no lib, no state.

plugins.name: seat-mods
plugins.description: Role guards for worker seats as a Claude Code mod: SEAT_MODS_ROLE on a seat's spawn turns on that role's tool-call rails; unset or empty, it guards as an implementer by default, and orchestrator and coordinator are explicit unguarded roles, except that on OMP an orchestrator may not spawn subagents.

plugins.name: molt
plugins.description: Context handoff as a Claude Code mod: warnings at 40% and 50% of the context window, a handoff command at 65% and a block at 75%; a root session is cleared in place and resumed from its handoff, a child session hands off to its parent.

plugins.name: autonomic
plugins.description: Autopilot as a Claude Code mod: standing orders in the system prompt; a cached fork judges each AskUserQuestion and permission ask against the policy and scope, never a turn end; a committed decision ledger; a closed pain list by toast, band and bell. Fails toward manual.

plugins.name: baton
plugins.description: A recipe-driven engine that launches model sessions on a host (T3 Code, or Orca terminals) when a unit is due, waits on closed signals at no token cost, and merges pull requests only by the recipe's rule; `baton answer` answers a worker's pending question by its exact label. Ships an example recipe that runs an ossify spine. A CLI, claim launchers and a systemd timer; no skill.

plugins.name: bot-on-telegram
plugins.description: Sends baton notices to one Telegram chat, with buttons, and turns button presses into baton actions. A CLI and a service; no skill.
